$comment: S1/DoD-1 -- the CHECK-STATUS vocabulary, shared across languages.
The rule it exists to carry: a guard that could not run must not be shaped like one
that ran and found nothing. Python has carried this as `loreweave_guard.CheckStatus`
since S1; Go and Rust generation paths carried it as a bare count, so a degraded sweep
and a clean sweep produced byte-identical output.
Python (sdks/python/loreweave_guard/__init__.py) is the SSOT. This file is generated
and every other language reads it in a drift test. Nothing reads it at runtime.
A language need not implement every member -- it must not INVENT one, and the members
it does use must rank the same way. `worst()` is the derived headline: WORST FIRST,
with not_applicable filtered out before ranking so 'out of scope' never drags a report
